Team memory: 2 note(s) about employee E011.
Note 1 (ticket 1):
  - role: Payroll Specialist (looked up in own database before writing)
  - employment type: full_time (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: write
  - comment: Richard Davis (E011) is a full-time Payroll Specialist. Requested write access to Payroll. Full-time employees can have up to write, and Payroll is owned by the Payroll Specialist role. Write is within policy, so recommend write.
Note 2 (ticket 1):
  - employment type: contractor (looked up in own database before writing)
  - security training: basic (looked up in own database before writing)
  - recommendation for Payroll: read
  - comment: Security DB shows Richard Davis (E011) is a contractor with basic security training (note this differs from the earlier note claiming full-time). Contractors never get admin; write requires advanced training. Since he has basic training, max access is read. Requested write exceeds max, so recommend read.

- contractor employees: read, or write if advanced security training. Never admin.

Given the security DB is specifically about contractors/training, and it explicitly notes the discrepancy, I lean toward the security info being reliable here. Contractor + basic training → max read. Requested write > max → grant read.

Also, the policy for contractors says write requires advanced security training. He has basic. So read.
